The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. This is a description of code behavior that is not in the supplied evidence (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift is not in this batch), so the claim is unverified here. The text is consistent with the existing T-041 posture: HMAC-keyed names, authenticated GCM, account-scoped cacheSalt, 30-minute TTL, and no new at-rest artifacts. The docs do not weaken any threat-model assumption.

The new live test uses an isolated ephemeral cache, an env -i scrubbed environment, and explicit variables. It measures cross-tenant restore timing under contention, which is relevant to the SEC-035 TTFT oracle, but it is a test of performance. It does not change the accepted-risk surface. The new test file itself is not supplied, so it was not reviewed. Test-report output paths are operator-chosen and may include prompt-derived timing, so no secret handling issue is visible in the docs.

Next-pass note: if the underlying code change (the unsupplied CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift host-bytes import and the staging scratch charge) lands in another batch, verify that the memory reservation and fail-closed behavior on authentication failure are preserved. The reservation covers staging scratch, and authentication of the entire file happens before use. No finding is recorded because the supplied evidence contains no code regression.
